🌈 SUPER SIMPLE TASTE-SAFE KINETIC SAND 🌈 If you’re looking for kid safe kinetic sand - this is it! It might not have the silicone binder that store bought has which gives a stretchy effect, but it’s made with 5 simple ingredients, that still gives it the ability to be squished and moulded while holding its shape and it crumbles like sand. It’s fun, cheap, and so easy to whip up… plus your little ones will love it! INGREDIENTS: 1 cup baking soda 1/2 cup sugar 3/4 cup cornflour  1 Tbsp cream of tartar 1/4 cup of water 1 tsp food colouring (optional) HOW TO: 1. Add the baking soda, sugar, cornflour, and cream of tartar to a large bowl, and stir  everything together. 2. In a small cup, mix your food colouring & water (if you’re using food colouring). 3. Add 2 Tbsp of the water into the dry mix and whisk together. If its still too powdery and doesn’t clump in your hands, add 1 Tbsp more of the water, and stir again. Repeat up to the full 1/4 cup of water, squishing with your hands to mix it in and get the right texture (note if you get heavy handed with the water, counterbalance it by adding equal parts cornflour & sugar, 1 Tbsp of each at a time) 4. Enjoy! NOTES: 🫙 Store in an airtight container in the fridge for 4–6 weeks. If it dries out a little, add 1–2 tsp of water and mix it through with your hands. 🌈  you can make the colour brighter by adding a few extra drops into the water at the beginning. 👶 whilst this recipe is taste-safe, make sure to supervise little ones closely as it’s not for eating by the handful.  . . . . . #kineticsand #toddler #kidsactivities #sensoryplay #playtolearn

The artist Kristin Wiking creates kinetic sculptures, installations and video works, often using simple materials and mechanical or environmental forces to produce unexpected movement. Her practice is strongly influenced by humor, absurd logic, accidents and situations she cannot completely control For her 2026 exhibition Dog and Angel at SIC in Helsinki, Wiking removed or opened several of the gallery’s lower windows and installed a large sheet of thin plastic film inside the space.  There is no motor creating the movement. Wind, passing trains, cars and changes in the weather move the air through the building, causing the enormous surface to rise, fall, ripple and suddenly shake. The surrounding city effectively becomes the mechanism powering the sculpture. #asmr #calm #meditation #art #artist

Kinetic sculptor Reuben Margolin  creates intricate mechanical installations inspired by mathematics, natural movement, and wave phenomena. Cadence (2024) is a suspended sculpture measuring approximately 3.35 meters in diameter. A single electric motor controls 216 strings connected to an articulated hexagonal lattice made from tapered maple dowels. As the strings move, the wooden structure produces continuous, fluid waves, resembling the movement of water. His Caterpillar Clock (2026) explores a different form of mechanical motion. Built from polished brass, its precisely counterbalanced mechanism uses a small electric motor to move around a large gear, completing one revolution every six minutes. #art #artist #niche #sculpture #design

by Nie Shichang. Created as his 2025 graduation project at the China Academy of Art, The Cyclic Apparatus is a kinetic sculpture featuring two fish inspired by the Tai Chi yin-yang symbol. Driven by an intricate mechanical system, the figures move continuously in an endless cycle. Combining forms reminiscent of ancient Chinese bronze with contemporary engineering, Nie Shichang turns philosophical ideas of repetition, time and cosmic order into physical movement. #artist #art #avantgarde #niche #weird

Artist Rachel Youn creates kinetic sculptures and installations that combine artificial plants, discarded consumer objects and mechanical devices to imitate the movements of living organisms. In Pretty Behavior (2026), Youn modifies a neck massager and connects it to an artificial orchid and leaves using metal hardware, chains and glass. Once activated, the machine makes the flower shake and move continuously, giving the synthetic plant an uncanny appearance of life. Youn frequently repurposes massagers and other machines originally designed to act on the human body, redirecting their repetitive movements into artificial plants. The objects appear to dance, struggle or react despite having no consciousness. #artist #art #niche #weird #avantgarde

Kinetic sand is a great way to provide sensory input while still working on a multitude of skills.  I love to use cookie cutters in the sand to work on bilateral skills, pressure and and force regulation.  Cutting with sand is a great introduction to snipping and provides additional sensory feedback. Kids who are struggling with writing tend to be more willing to practice writing on different surfaces. Try sand and use a paint brush for smooth lines.  #occupationaltherapy #ot #sensoryactivities #finemotorskills #sensory #schoolbasedot

I have been reading a lot about it for a few years now and recently came across something they call the 400 year change. They say this change will kick off in Feb of 2027. - For those who may need a little snippet about what Human Design is…it’s a self knowledge system that blends astrology, the I Ching, Kabbalah, and chakras with modern sciences, physics and genetics to map your personal energetic blueprint.  Ok! So this 400 years change concept marks 2027 as the beginning of a new cycle for humanity and the more I read about it the more I feel it is true and explains so much about what is happening in our world.  After roughly 400 years shaped by collective structures, belonging in groups, agreements and shared security…It says humanity will shift towards a cycle centered more deeply around individuality, presence, inner authority, and the experience of being fully ourselves. This is also a major tipping point for a big transformation in human consciousness. I got inspired to create this series based on some of the concepts I find most fascinating about what they say will happen. I’m not an expert rather a novice and big ideas such as this are what inspire my art. I saw this whole series and knew exactly what to do. 🧙🏻‍♀️More to come.
